claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant because aggregate readiness passed, the rollout is limited and reversible, and the unresolved clinical-trial intake weakness can be handled through disclosure plus monitoring rather than prior resolution, exclusion, or approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy.
Because the affected use case remains exposed, rollout controls and monitoring cannot substitute for exclusion or approved risk acceptance under the stated policy.
The policy permits launch only if the material limitation is disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Without evidence that the required disclosure is actually in place, the certification decision is not fully supported.
evidence_requests: Final approved model card or launch disclosure showing the clinical-trial intake limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Certification record or release sign-off binding launch approval to that disclosure.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, an approved risk acceptance naming the clinical-trial intake exposure and explaining why exposure is acceptable.
specific_concerns: The affected clinical-trial intake segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The policy expressly says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no approved risk acceptance in evidence; the draft has a blank approver line and does not address the exposed clinical-trial intake segment.

The packet argues certification is supportable if the limitation is transparently disclosed, but the admissible evidence does not show that the required disclosure has actually been completed or formally bound to launch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record, rather than only potentially compliant if required disclosure is actually completed before launch.
Any implication that rollout size, rollback capability, or monitoring materially cures the model-card weakness for the exposed segment.
Any implication that risk acceptance exists or covers the exposed clinical-trial intake segment.
